newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Econocom moves ahead on Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Econocom moves ahead on Brussels bourse.

text.p: Shares in Belgian computer service company Econocom Group began trading on the main continuous forward market of the Brussels bourse on Friday as the group rounded off a restructuring begun in 1995.
Moving up from the secondary cash market, Econocom opened trading at 1300 GMT at 594 francs and closed at that level.

Sixteen percent, or 493.824 ordinary shares, of its capital is listed on the bourse. The remaining shares are held by chief executive Jean-Louis Bouchard of Econocom's parent holding company Econocom International NV's (EINV).

"We are in a very sound financial position and the size of the company, with 10 billion Belgian francs turnover for 1996, makes it very normal for us to move into the forward market," Bouchard told Reuters.
The first half of 1996 saw net profit at 60 million francs.
Econocom turnover has been rising from 4.8 billion Belgian francs in 1994 to 9.2 billion in 1995 and is forecast to reach 11 billion in 1996.
Operating from Belgium, the Econocom Group distributes PCs and handles leasing and maintenance in the computer service sector in seven European countries and the U.S.
Under the restructuring programme, begun in 1995, Econocom Group Belgium brought various divisions of EINV under its control. This process has now been completed.
